additional_info.subject: 0480088 - ID0480088-DC/Si-D/BE- [Multi] Persistent Connectivity Issue CRM:02582000005
additional_info.body:
Recently the CCS2 plug was replaced by customer for Zm5QuW this charger in
ID0477339
The CP wire internal of the CCS2 plug was found to have a high resistance and caused the CP voltage to drop. Due to this finding the CCS2 cable was replaced.
5 days after replacing the CCS2 cable it has become defective again. Because of the following findings I doubt that replacing the CCS2 cable again will solve the issue for long term. Is this a known issue/possibility that the ECOG breaks the PT1000 and CP line of the CCS2 cable?
W
hen I measure the outlet 2 CP wire (CP wire in X16) to the CCS2 plug, I measure 35-45k ohms. Compared this with outlet 1, should be 0 ohm. See pictures.
Also a CableTempSensor error is active in SCB. I removed the CCS2 PT1000 sensors at X16 and measured the resistance of the Pt1000 and compared the values with outlet 1 of the same charger.
Finding is that the PT1000 P1(BU)-N1(WH) is 240Ohm. Which is low compared to the other PT1000 values of around 1,5kOhm up to 2,5kOhm in this charger.
241 Ohm on outlet 2 PT1000 (BLUE-WHITE)
Measured 2,15kOhm on working outlet 1 (BLUE-WHITE)

additional_info.subject: RE: 0480088 - ID0480088-DC/Si-D/BE- [Multi] Persistent Connectivity Issue CRM:02582000005
additional_info.body:
Hello Bart,
Your measurement's are not being made in the proper way.
The schematic could lead to a wrong conclusion when we see the + ans -. It's not the + and - of the PT1000. In this case the + and - means the DC pins polarity.
Measurements need to be done from
Blue with orange
White and violet
For both are expected values around 1000 ohm to 1100 ohm, depending on the ambient temperature.
There is no known issue of ecog breaking the PT1000 in the plugs. You can always review the connections in the charger to be sure that everything is correct.
For the CP your are correct, we expect to measure a very low resistance value.
Please confirm the values and if is really out of the expected range replace the cable.
I can't do any troubleshoot since the charger is offline, I will send back this ticket to your queue.
If any support is needed from my side, feel free to reach out to me via TEAMS.
With best regards,
Joao Francisco Louro Cardoso

additional_info.subject: Site visit
additional_info.body:
Performed hard reset, charger came online in SCB. Downloaded logs in case it goes offline again. See attachment.
This is the second CCS cable that has been broken on outlet 2. Original and this CCS cable both had 1 working charge session before they broke. CP line/wire resistance in both cases increased and pulls down CP voltage. First ticket
ID0477339
W
hen I measure the outlet 2 CP wire (CP wire in X16) to the CCS2 plug, I measure 35-45k ohms. Compared this with outlet 1, should be 0 ohm. See pictures in previous note.
Plug2 PT1000 measurements
PT1000 resistance P1-P2 blue-orange: 1,041k Ohm
PT1000 resistance N1-N2 white-violet: 149 Ohm
CP voltage on plug B connector is measured as 7.6V DC
Compared the KF14 voltages between J4 and J5.
1) Why do I measure 6,6V on PP of J5? on J4 this is 0V
2) PT2 voltage on J5 is low because PT2 resistance is measured as 149 Ohm.
J4: CP 12V PP 0V PT1: 1,09V PT2 1,09V
J5: CP 7,6V PP 6,6V PT1: 1,09V PT2 0,3V
My assuption since this is the second broken CCS2 cable on outlet 2 is that there is something wrong with internal KF14 J5. The cabling on J5 is correct.

additional_info.subject: 0480088 - ID0480088-DC/Si-D/BE- [Multi] CP line resistance and issues on cables CRM:00472000566
additional_info.body:
Hello Bart,
After Bas Jeurissen's intervention today, those are the findings:
The PT1000 on the Negative pin from CCS plug is defective (very low resistance), the CCS cable need to be replaced.
The CP Voltage is below whats is expected from Pilot state A (12V), and there is voltage applied on the PP line when shouldn't be. Please proceed with the replacement of State monitor KF14.
For the connectivity issue I recommend running for 2 weeks, a trial with the ORANGE network provider (same used by OCPP), to see if this change would increase the charger SCB communication stability.
With best regards,
